positions.source_passage: We strongly support CDRH’s competency-based evaluation model (integrating standardized benchmarking with risk-tiered clinical confirmation) and urge the Agency to ensure clear, streamlined pathways for high-impact use cases:
positions.position_gist: Commenter endorses the competency-based evaluation model combining standardized benchmarking with risk-tiered clinical confirmation, and urges streamlined pathways for high-impact use cases.

positions.source_passage: Two-Axis Risk Calibration (Questions 1–6): Anchor ambient scribing, EHR screening, and HCP-supervised imaging second-reads firmly in lower-risk categories, reserving high-intensity premarket scrutiny for unmonitored autonomous execution.
positions.position_gist: The risk framework should place ambient scribing, EHR screening, and HCP-supervised imaging second-reads in lower-risk categories, reserving intensive premarket scrutiny for unmonitored autonomous execution.

positions.source_passage: Competency Benchmarking (Questions 7–10): Prioritize Safety Escalation (S.1) and Quantitative Analysis (E.3) to guarantee numerical precision and prevent confabulations in blood lab analysis.
positions.position_gist: Within the benchmarking structure, FDA should prioritize the Safety Escalation (S.1) and Quantitative Analysis (E.3) competencies to ensure numerical precision and prevent confabulation in blood lab analysis.

positions.source_passage: Voluntary Master Files (Question 25): Fully operationalize Foundation Model Device Master Files (MAFs) so downstream developers can leverage upstream model cards without exposing proprietary weights.
positions.position_gist: FDA should fully operationalize voluntary Foundation Model Master Files so downstream developers can rely on upstream model cards without disclosure of proprietary weights.

positions.source_passage: Postmarket Monitoring (Questions 18–24): Enable machine-based supervisory agents and flexible Predetermined Change Control Plans (PCCPs) under FD&C Act § 515C to govern model drift without requiring burdensome supplemental clearances.
positions.position_gist: FDA should permit machine-based supervisory agents for postmarket monitoring and flexible PCCPs under FD&C Act § 515C to manage model drift without requiring burdensome supplemental clearances.

positions.source_passage: FDA should advance this discussion paper into formal Draft Guidance, establishing streamlined clearance pathways for HCP-supervised AI tools while operationalizing the Foundation Model MAF program to accelerate safe, life-saving healthcare innovation.
positions.position_gist: FDA should convert the discussion paper into formal draft guidance that includes streamlined clearance pathways for HCP-supervised AI tools and an operational Foundation Model MAF program.
